page: Google Cloud Platform a3-highgpu-8g is an accelerator-optimized server configured with eight NVIDIA H100 GPUs from the Hopper family, providing a total of 640 GB of VRAM. The host system is powered by Intel Xeon 8481C processors using the x86_64 architecture, delivering 208 dedicated vCPUs across 104 physical cores with a base clock speed of 2.7 GHz. The system includes 1872.0 GB of system memory, translating to 9.0 GB per core, and is equipped with 6167 GB of local NVMe SSD storage.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier performance across multiple domains. Multi-core CPU performance via stress-ng and PassMark CPU tests ranks in the top 10%, aided by advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions. Memory bandwidth is exceptionally high, with both small-block cached and large-block uncached read operations placing in the top 10%. Storage and database capabilities are similarly positioned, with Redis SET operations and static web serving throughput achieving top-tier results. Single-core CPU performance and PassMark memory scores represent a relative tradeoff, landing in the middle 50% average tier.

Given the high density of hardware accelerators and massive system memory, this server is designed for large-scale parallel processing tasks. It is optimized for large language model training and inference, data science pipelines, and complex physics simulations. Qualitative cost efficiency is characterized by the high consolidation of GPU and CPU resources on a single node, reducing the network overhead typically associated with multi-node clusters.
